Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testLang295` creates a StrBuilder with the string "onetwothree" and then calls `deleteFirst("three")`. After deleting the first occurrence of "three", it asserts that the `contains(char)` method should not find the character 'h'. The test expects this to be false since "three" was removed, so 'h' should not be present.

Examining `StrBuilder.deleteFirst(String)`, it finds the index of the substring and calls `deleteImpl` to remove those characters, adjusting the internal size appropriately.

The `contains(char ch)` method implementation reveals the issue: it iterates over the entire `buffer` array using `thisBuf.length`. This length represents the capacity of the internal character buffer, not the current content size (which is stored in the `size` field). Thus, `contains` may check beyond the current logical end of the string and find the character 'h' in leftover buffer contents not part of the current string, causing a false positive.

The bug report confirms this is a misuse of `thisBuf.length` and suggests that size-limited iteration should be used in `StrBuilder` methods to avoid such errors leading to incorrect results or array index exceptions.

In summary, the bug occurs because the `contains(char)` method scans all of the internal buffer `thisBuf` including unused/empty positions beyond the actual string length `size`, thereby reporting characters mistakenly. This causes the test failure as the 'h' character is found in unused buffer space after deleting "three".

Fixing this requires changing `contains(char)` (and similar methods using `thisBuf.length`) to iterate only up to the logical current size of the string `size` instead of the entire buffer array length.

The recent bug reports do not provide directly relevant information besides confirming the theme of bugs around incorrect string manipulations; they can be ignored here. The key issue lies in misusing `thisBuf.length` instead of `size` in `contains`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
